items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: Well you’re saying what Jerry Bergonzi said this thing almost off hand... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. That’s the truth. That’s a nice light way of putting it you know. But it is, it’s true. You know I never had to do that. And he was a great teacher so –

ctx.x: Yeah it’s not good news unfortunately. I tell them, you know if they’re heading into college to definitely search out another degree to do something else than performance. Because performing live music is almost impossible today. You know if you get into a great school, you know one of the great schools, Eastman or Berklee or Texas – Denton, Texas – you know you’ll meet – network people you know, and maybe that way you could you know hook up for some great gigs, some concerts and stuff like that. And it’s lucky.…
Well you’re saying what Jerry Bergonzi said this thing almost off hand, he just said, “Well you have to have a job to support your gigs.”

Yeah. That’s the truth. That’s a nice light way of putting it you know. But it is, it’s true. You know I never had to do that. And he was a great teacher so – and that’s what most guys do now is teaching. You know so they’re in the university teaching and I don't know, the young guys – there’s some unbelievable young musicians. They have so much maturity at such a young age. And you know they blow my mind a lot of times at how much they know. And we’re talking about tune knowledge. They know a ton of tunes as…
